label: Window itself
summary: The memories window itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the window so other functions can use it. The game's documentation gives no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this window.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the memories window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the memories window. It returns nothing.

label: Copy memories
summary: Copies the window's memories to the clipboard.
details: Going by its name, it puts the memories on the clipboard. Vanilla calls it from a button click in the memories window. It returns nothing.

label: Window character
summary: The character whose memories the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it in the window's heading and info text: it checks whether the character exists and, if so, writes their short name in the possessive form ("X's Memories"). Without a valid character the text says "No" or "lost".

label: Filtered memories
summary: The list of memories left after the window's filters are applied.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list that fills the window's memory rows. It also checks whether the list is empty to show an empty-state message.

label: Has required category
summary: Whether a given memory category is one of the categories the window currently requires.
details: Going by its name and its yes/no return, it checks the filter state of one category. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: List is descending
summary: Whether the memories list is sorted in descending order.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick which of two frames (images) of the sort button is shown, so the button reflects the order.

label: Window is pinned
summary: Whether the memories window is pinned.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the window, for example the pin button's two looks.

label: Window itself
summary: The memories window itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the window for use as an argument to other functions. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this window. The same name on other types is used that way, for example `CHARACTER.Self`.

label: Flip list order
summary: Switches the memories list between ascending and descending order.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the memories window. It returns nothing.

label: Pin window
summary: Pins the memories window if it is loose, or unpins it if it is pinned.
details: Vanilla calls it from two pin buttons in the window. They are shown depending on `IsPinned`. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle category
summary: Switches a memory category on or off in the window's category filter.
details: Going by its name, it adds the category to the required ones or removes it. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it. It returns nothing.

label: Memory itself
summary: The memory object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the memory so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Participants text
summary: A text naming the participants of the memory.
details: Going by its name, it builds a list of the people involved. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Memory name
summary: The memory's name as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the debug watch window to label a memory. The same function name exists on many other types and returns their names.

label: Debug scopes
summary: A debug text about the scopes of the memory.
details: Going by its name, it is a developer aid. A similar call on another type is used as a tooltip in the debug watch window. Vanilla does not use this exact one.

label: Memory tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the memory.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a memory entry in the debug watch window.

label: Memory itself
summary: The memory object itself.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the memory for use as an argument to other functions. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Type itself
summary: The men-at-arms type itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the type so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Fights in main phase
summary: Whether this men-at-arms type fights in the main phase of combat.
details: Going by its name, it is a yes/no check on the type. Vanilla uses it to show or hide a "counters" text in the levy window and parts of the men-at-arms type view.

label: Base type name
summary: The name of the base type of this men-at-arms type.
details: Going by its name, it gives the name of the type this one is based on. Vanilla uses it in the "Type: ..." line of the military view and in a map tooltip that lists troops per type.

label: Cost text
summary: A text showing what a regiment of this men-at-arms type costs the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the player and uses it in the creation-cost and size-increase tooltips. It shows plain regiment costs; for a title-held regiment the game uses `GetTitleRegimentCostString` instead.

label: Counters text
summary: A text listing the unit types this men-at-arms type counters.
details: Vanilla uses it in a tooltip that begins with the type's name followed by "counters these Types:".

label: Creation cost text
summary: A text showing what creating this men-at-arms type costs the given character.
details: Going by its name, it is like `GetCostString` but about creation. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Flavor text
summary: The descriptive flavor text of this men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text line in the men-at-arms window and in the type view.

label: Full maintenance text
summary: A text showing the maintenance cost of this type at full strength for the player.
details: Vanilla uses it in the size-change tooltips and in the type view, which switches to the title version when a title is selected.

label: Holding modifiers
summary: The list of holding modifiers of this men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list for a section of the type view, and hides that section when the list is empty.

label: Wide image
summary: The wide (horizontal) picture of this men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in a tooltip. For a culture-specific picture the game has `GetHorizontalImageForCulture`.

label: Wide image for culture
summary: The wide picture of this men-at-arms type as shown for the given culture.
details: Vanilla passes the player's culture, or the culture of a regiment's owner, and uses the result as a texture in the accolade and men-at-arms windows.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture whose look to use.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of this men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the accolade, army and battle summary windows.

label: Icon key
summary: A short key text for this type's icon.
details: Vanilla builds an inline icon from it in the form `@KEY_icon!` inside texts, for example in hints about recruiting from subjects.

label: Max fort level
summary: The highest fort level this men-at-arms type is effective against, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in a siege tooltip: "Effective up to fort level N".

label: Name
summary: The name of this men-at-arms type as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in recruitment texts and effect descriptions, with a tooltip on the name.

label: Name, no tooltip
summary: The name of this men-at-arms type as plain text, without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in battle summary lines such as "Counters X" and in the counters tooltip.

label: Province stat
summary: The number for one combat stat of this type in a given province, as the game computes it.
details: Vanilla asks for the stats damage, toughness and pursuit, and shows the result as a signed number. It passes the player, the province, the title and the stat name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the stat is for.

label: Province stat text
summary: A text describing one combat stat of this type in a province.
details: Vanilla uses it under the heading of the damage, toughness and pursuit tooltips of a province.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the stat is for.

label: Provisions cost text
summary: A text showing the provisions cost of this men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla shows it in the type view and in a shared tooltip.

label: Reinforcement cost text
summary: A text showing the reinforcement cost of this men-at-arms type for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it in the size-change tooltips, after the lines "Maintenance will increase by" and "Maintenance will be reduced by". The title version is `GetTitleRegimentReinforcementCostString`.

label: Stack size
summary: How many soldiers one size step of this men-at-arms type holds, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as "Soldiers per Size" and the starting size note when creating a regiment.

label: Stack size text
summary: The stack size of this men-at-arms type as text.
details: Going by its name, it is the text form of `GetStackSize`. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Stat
summary: The value of one combat stat of this type for a given province and title.
details: Vanilla asks for damage, toughness and pursuit and shows the result in tooltips next to `GetStatDesc`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the stat is for.

label: Stat text
summary: A text explaining how one combat stat of this type is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it in the damage, toughness and pursuit tooltips, below the number from `GetStat`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the stat is for.

label: Subject hint text
summary: A hint text about getting this men-at-arms type from a subject.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip of the create button for a type. Going by the surrounding texts, it explains that a subject could provide the type.

label: Subject provider
summary: The subject who gives the given character access to this men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla checks whether the result is valid and writes it into the text "Access to X is provided by ...".

label: Terrain modifiers
summary: The list of terrain modifiers of this men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list for a section of the type view, and hides that section when the list is empty.

label: Title regiment cost text
summary: A text showing what a title regiment of this type costs the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it when a title is selected in the type view, and in the creation-cost tooltip of title regiments.

label: Title creation cost text
summary: A text showing the creation cost of a title regiment of this type.
details: Going by its name, it is the creation version of the title regiment cost text. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Title full maintenance text
summary: A text showing the full-strength maintenance cost of a title regiment of this type for the player.
details: Vanilla uses it in the title versions of the size-change tooltips and in the type view when a title is selected.

label: Title reinforcement text
summary: A text showing the reinforcement cost of a title regiment of this type for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it in the title versions of the size-change tooltips and in the type view when a title is selected.

label: Tall image
summary: The tall (vertical) picture of this men-at-arms type.
details: Going by its name, it is the vertical counterpart of `GetHorizontalImage`. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Tall image for culture
summary: The tall picture of this men-at-arms type as shown for the given culture.
details: Going by its name, it is the vertical counterpart of `GetHorizontalImageForCulture`. Vanilla uses a call on another path, a regiment's type in the battle summary window, with the culture of a battle side's main participant.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture whose look to use.

label: Harsh winter modifier
summary: The modifier this men-at-arms type gets in a harsh winter.
details: Vanilla shows its effect text in a tooltip headed "In Harsh Winter" and checks whether it is positive to pick the look of the entry.

label: Normal winter modifier
summary: The modifier this men-at-arms type gets in a normal winter.
details: Vanilla shows its effect text in a tooltip headed "In Normal Winter" and checks whether it is positive to pick the look of the entry.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether this men-at-arms type has an icon.
details: Going by its name, it is a yes/no check. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it on this type, only the same name on other types in a shared tooltip.

label: Has harsh winter modifier
summary: Whether this men-at-arms type has a modifier for harsh winters.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the harsh winter part of the type view.

label: Has normal winter modifier
summary: Whether this men-at-arms type has a modifier for normal winters.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the normal winter part of the type view.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether there is a real men-at-arms type here.
details: Vanilla uses it in the accolade window to show an element only when a type exists. Many other types have an `IsValid` of the same kind.

label: Type itself
summary: The men-at-arms type itself, as an object to pass on.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument, for example to the battle summary window when it asks for the types a type counters or is countered by.

label: View itself
summary: The men-at-arms type view itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the view so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Can create
summary: Whether a regiment of the selected type can be created now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the create button in the type view.

label: Close view
summary: Closes the men-at-arms type view.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the view. It returns nothing.

label: Create regiment
summary: Creates a regiment of the selected men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla calls it from the create button of the type view. It returns nothing. `CanCreate` tells whether it is possible.

label: Cost text
summary: A text showing what the selected type costs the given character.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text line in the type view.

label: Create tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the create button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the first part of the "can create" tooltip, followed by hints about subjects who may provide the type.

label: Types list
summary: The list of men-at-arms types the view shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list that fills the type rows of the view.

label: Selected type
summary: The men-at-arms type currently selected in the view.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the view's detail area, so everything in it works on the selected type.

label: Selected title
summary: The title selected in the view, if any.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for a title part of the view and checks whether it is valid. When it is, the cost lines switch to the title-regiment versions.

label: View title
summary: The heading text of the view.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the type view.

label: A type is selected
summary: Whether a men-at-arms type is selected in the view.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the detail area when something is selected and a hint when nothing is.

label: Is using horde
summary: Whether the view is in horde mode.
details: Going by its name, it is a yes/no check. Vanilla uses it, together with a check for the landless adventurer government, to decide which parts of the type view are shown.

label: View itself
summary: The men-at-arms type view itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the view for use as an argument. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Item itself
summary: The type row of the type view, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the row so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Can create
summary: Whether a regiment of this row's type can be created.
details: Vanilla uses it negated: when creating is not possible it shows the warning and its tooltip.

label: Create warning
summary: The text that says why this row's type cannot be created.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip, shown when creating is not possible.

label: Row's type
summary: The men-at-arms type this row stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the row, so the row's content works on that type.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this row is the selected one in the type view.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed (down) state of the row's button.

label: Select row
summary: Selects this row's men-at-arms type in the view.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click and when an animation finishes. Going by its name and these uses, it makes the row the selection. It returns nothing.

label: Item itself
summary: The type row of the type view, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the row for use as an argument. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: View itself
summary: The men-at-arms regiment view itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the view so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Buy regiment
summary: Buys the men-at-arms regiment shown in the view.
details: Going by its name and its use, it is called from a button in the men-at-arms window. `CanBuyMaa` tells whether the button is allowed. It returns nothing.

label: Can buy
summary: Whether the regiment shown can be bought.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the buy button and to switch between the buy and sell parts of the window.

label: Can change origin province
summary: Whether the origin province of the regiment can be changed.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the button that opens the origin province selection.

label: Can destroy
summary: Whether the regiment shown can be destroyed.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the destroy button.

label: Can sell
summary: Whether the regiment shown can be sold.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the sell button and to switch between the sell and buy parts of the window.

label: Close view
summary: Closes the men-at-arms window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the window. It returns nothing.

label: Destroy regiment
summary: Destroys the men-at-arms regiment shown in the view.
details: Going by its name, it destroys the regiment. Vanilla calls it from a button click in the men-at-arms window. `CanDestroyMaa` is used to enable a button there. It returns nothing.

label: Origin province tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the origin province button.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip. Going by its name, it explains whether and why the origin province can be changed.

label: Decrease size tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for making the regiment smaller.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the men-at-arms window.

label: Full strength text
summary: A text line about the regiment's full-strength state.
details: Vanilla puts it above the line "Paying Full maintenance" or "Paying Unraised maintenance" in maintenance tooltips.

label: Increase size blockers
summary: A text listing what stops the regiment from growing.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the men-at-arms window. Going by its name, it names the reasons.

label: Increase size tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for making the regiment bigger.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the men-at-arms window.

label: Reduce size blockers
summary: A text listing what stops the regiment from shrinking.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in two places of the men-at-arms window. Going by its name, it names the reasons.

label: Regiment
summary: The regiment the view shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window, so the window's content works on this regiment.

label: Choose origin province
summary: Opens the selection of the regiment's origin province.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on the origin province button. It returns nothing. `CanChangeOriginProvince` is used to enable a button in the same window.

label: Remove origin province
summary: Removes the regiment's chosen origin province.
details: Going by its name, it clears the choice. Vanilla calls it on a right click of the origin province button. It returns nothing.

label: View itself
summary: The men-at-arms regiment view itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the view for use as an argument. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Sell regiment
summary: Sells the men-at-arms regiment shown in the view.
details: Going by its name, it is called from a button click in the men-at-arms window. `CanSellMaa` tells whether the button is allowed. It returns nothing.

label: Company itself
summary: The mercenary company itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the company so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Can be raised
summary: Whether the mercenary company can be raised.
details: Vanilla combines it with a check that the local player hired the company, to enable the raise button of the hired troops detail window.

label: Cost text
summary: A text describing what hiring the company costs.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the military window and, per another line, inside a hire info text next to the hire duration.

label: Culture
summary: The culture of the mercenary company.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives a culture object. Vanilla does not use it on this type.

label: Current soldiers
summary: How many soldiers the company has now, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the hired troops list and the title view as "N soldiers", and uses it with the maximum for a progress bar.

label: Hire duration text
summary: A text describing how long the company is hired for.
details: Vanilla uses it through a hired troop item in a text that reads like "cost for a duration".

label: Time left
summary: How much hire time is left for the company, as a text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the hired troops view as "... left".

label: Home county
summary: The county the mercenary company is based in.
details: Going by its name, it gives the home county. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Home county title
summary: The title of the county the mercenary company is based in.
details: Going by its name, it gives the title of the home county. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Max soldiers
summary: The most soldiers the company can have, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it with the current number to fill a progress bar in the title window.

label: Name
summary: The name of the mercenary company as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the military window and in the tooltip of a hired troops list button.

label: Number of knights
summary: How many knights the company has, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in the title view next to a knight icon, labelled with the holy order holder's word for knights.

label: Owner
summary: The character who owns the mercenary company.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives a character. Vanilla does not use it on this type.

label: Soldiers ratio
summary: The share of soldiers the company has, in the form a progress bar wants.
details: Going by its name, it is a ready value for a progress bar. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it; they build the bar from current and maximum soldiers instead.

label: Company title
summary: The title the mercenary company is tied to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of an army window, and its holder as the context in the military window. The game documents no return type.

label: Is hired
summary: Whether the mercenary company is currently hired by someone.
details: Vanilla uses it in the military window to choose which hire buttons and tooltips are shown.

label: Hired by me
summary: Whether the company is hired by the player at this computer.
details: Vanilla uses it with `IsHired` and `CanBeRaised` to decide which buttons are enabled or visible. The game documents no return type, but it is used as a yes/no value.

label: As scope
summary: The company as a script scope, so script values and checks can be run on it.
details: Going by its type (a scope) and the same name on other types, it turns the object into one script can work with. Vanilla does not use it on this type.

label: Company itself
summary: The mercenary company itself, as an object to pass on.
details: Vanilla passes it to functions that raise a company or check whether its detail view is shown.

label: Would cause bankruptcy
summary: Whether hiring the company would drive the given character into bankruptcy.
details: Vanilla passes the player and uses it to choose between hire buttons and warnings in the military window.

label: Would cause debt
summary: Whether hiring the company would put the given character in debt.
details: Vanilla passes the player and uses it with `IsHired` and `WillGoInBankruptcy` to choose which hire warning is shown.

label: Item itself
summary: The merit item itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the item so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Character
summary: The character the merit item belongs to.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives a character. Vanilla does not use it on this type.

label: Complex bar
summary: The data of the merit bar shown in the HUD.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a bar in the HUD. Going by its name, it carries what that bar needs.

label: Current level
summary: The merit level reached now, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla passes it to a function that turns a level into its short name for the HUD text.

label: Current rank
summary: The merit rank reached now, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name, it is the rank counterpart of the level. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the merit item.
details: Going by its name and the same name on other types, it gives a description text. Vanilla does not use it on this type.

label: Leftover space factor
summary: A whole number used as a layout stretch factor for the leftover space of the merit bar.
details: Going by its name, it sets how much room the unfilled part takes. Vanilla uses it as a horizontal layout stretch factor in the HUD bar.

label: Levels
summary: The list of levels of the merit item.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data list in the HUD.

label: Merit width factor
summary: A whole number used as a layout stretch factor for the earned merit in the merit bar.
details: Going by its name, it sets how much room the earned merit takes. Vanilla uses it as a horizontal layout stretch factor in the HUD bar.

label: Overflow width factor
summary: A whole number used as a layout stretch factor for the overflow part of the merit bar.
details: Going by its name, the overflow is merit beyond the top level. Vanilla uses it as a horizontal layout stretch factor and shows the overflow part only when it is greater than 0.

label: Progress
summary: How far the merit item has progressed, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a progress bar in the HUD.

label: Value item
summary: The value object tied to the merit item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of an element in the HUD. The game documents no return type.

label: Item itself
summary: The merit item itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the item for use as an argument. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Window itself
summary: The merit pool window itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the window so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the merit pool window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click and when the government administration window starts. It returns nothing.

label: Merit item
summary: The merit item at the given position of the list.
details: Vanilla passes the index of the current list row of the government administration window and uses the result as that row's data context.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, such as CharacterListItem.GetIndex

label: Score
summary: The appointment score of the candidate at the given position.
details: Vanilla shows it with an appointment score icon in the government administration window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, such as CharacterListItem.GetIndex

label: Score breakdown
summary: The breakdown of the succession score of a character.
details: Vanilla passes the character of a list row and uses the result as a data context in the government administration window.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the merit pool window is shown.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the government administration window.

label: Scroll to candidate
summary: Scrolls the list to the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the character and the number 15 on a click. Going by the name, the second value is how far or how many rows to scroll with; the game does not say. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A whole number; vanilla uses 15. Its exact meaning is not documented.

label: Window itself
summary: The merit pool window itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the window for use as an argument. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Show window
summary: Shows the merit pool window.
details: Going by its name, it opens the window. Vanilla does not use it on this type. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle window
summary: Shows the merit pool window if it is hidden, or hides it if it is shown.
details: Going by its name, it switches the window. Vanilla does not use it on this type. It returns nothing.

label: Handler itself
summary: The message feed handler itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the handler so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Close feed
summary: Closes the message feed.
details: Going by its name, it closes the feed. Vanilla does not use it on this type. It returns nothing.

label: Feed items
summary: The list of messages in the feed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of the message templates in the HUD.

label: Queued messages
summary: How many messages wait in the queue, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text "N more messages".

label: Has queued messages
summary: Whether any messages wait in the queue.
details: Going by its name, it is the yes/no form of the queue count. Vanilla's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Dismiss all messages
summary: Marks all messages in the feed for removal.
details: Vanilla calls it on a left and a right click of a feed element. Going by its name, the messages then disappear. It returns nothing.

label: Handler itself
summary: The message feed handler itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the handler for use as an argument. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Item itself
summary: The message filter item itself, as an object.
details: Going by its name, it hands out the item so other functions can use it. The game documents no return type, and vanilla does not use it for this type.

label: Hovered index
summary: The grid position of the filter cell the mouse is over, as a pair of whole numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected index in the message settings window.
